bullets.title: Let Things Rot
bullets.note: from the [Fungi Foundation](https://ffungi.org/). This is gorgeously shot, and it’s worth a five-minute break for the visuals alone. From the description: “The Fungi Foundation is proud to present ‘Let Things Rot,’ a new documentary short directed by [Mateo Barrenengoa](https://www.mateobarrenengoa.cl/) in collaboration with mycologist and foundation founder [Giuliana Furci](https://tim.blog/2021/07/29/giuliana-furci/?utm_source=convertkit&utm_medium=convertkit&utm_campaign=5bf) \[[@giulifungi](https://www.instagram.com/giulifungi/?hl=en)\]. Filmed in Chile’s Araucanía Region, the short delves into fungi’s crucial role as a decomposer, inviting the viewer to reconsider rotting through a new, poetic perspective.”

bullets.title: Language Lessons
bullets.note: This is the first movie I’ve seen in theaters since COVID. It is (e)spectacular! The format is genius, the characters are gorgeously imperfect, and the emotions are exactly what I needed. Highest recommendation. Kudos to [Natalie Morales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natalie_Morales_(actress)) ([@nataliemorales](https://twitter.com/nataliemorales)), [Mark Duplass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Duplass) ([@MarkDuplass](https://twitter.com/markduplass)), and the entire team. Pro tip: Don’t watch the trailer or read descriptions, as they contain too many possible spoilers. Enjoy the laughs and catharsis.

bullets.title: How We Got Our Grid and How We Get a Better One
bullets.note: [Click here to skip directly to the start of the episode at 5:52](https://open.spotify.com/episode/1rzbM5eYENDdqAb4yQM3Yk?si=KQpQelyXQ-2_ewogb-gXbA&context=spotify%3Aepisode%3A1rzbM5eYENDdqAb4yQM3Yk&t=352&dl_branch=1). Description: “Wind and solar are now some of the cheapest ways to make electricity. So what’s standing in the way of using more of these renewable energies? One of the biggest barriers is something all around us that we rarely notice—our electricity grid. Not just the wires and technology that make up the grid but also the people and institutions that run it. In this episode, we talk with anthropologist [Gretchen Bakke](https://bakkeconsolidated.org/), author of [_The Grid: The Fraying Wires Between Americans and Our Energy Future_](https://www.amazon.com/Grid-Fraying-Between-Americans-Energy/dp/1632865688/), about how we got our grid and how we get a better one.”
